answer: The glacier report reveals the merge explicitly at each copper. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 266 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 298 times the capital for one share. That is 25 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
